basis: CMS requires a qualifying covered retiree for RDS to be eligible for Medicare Part D but not enrolled in a Part D plan. RDS therefore represents employer/union retiree-drug subsidy payments outside the ordinary Part D plan-payment stream reconstructed by WCFFBP.

RDS is a prescription-drug subsidy to qualified retiree plan sponsors. Original Medicare/FFS accounting represents the certified Part A/B FFS payment stream. A retiree may participate in Original Medicare while also being covered by an RDS-qualified employer/union drug plan, but the federal payment streams are economically distinct.

Certified Part C accounting consists of Medicare Advantage A/B plan payment plus Part C rebate. RDS is a separate prescription-drug subsidy paid under the employer/union retiree-drug subsidy program. No RDS component is included in the certified WCFFBP Part C reconstruction.
